question: Which levels of government in Nigeria are responsible for managing the three-tier system of healthcare delivery?

options.C: Private sectors and traditional rulers only

explanation: The Nigerian healthcare system is structured into a three-tier system managed respectively by local, state, and federal governments. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is identified as a major factor that severely restricts healthcare access for millions of Nigerians?

options.B: Widespread poverty and high out-of-pocket spending
options.C: An overabundance of rural health facilities

explanation: Socioeconomic challenges such as widespread poverty and high out-of-pocket spending severely restrict healthcare access for millions of Nigerians. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is one of the primary purposes of policies like the National Health Act in Nigeria?

options.A: To dissolve all local health clinics
options.B: To establish legal frameworks for universal health coverage and regulate standards
options.C: To privatize all federal tertiary hospitals

explanation: Policies such as the National Health Act are designed to establish legal frameworks for universal health coverage, regulate health standards, and define government responsibilities. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why do comprehensive health policies in Nigeria often fail to translate into tangible clinical improvements?

options.A: Due to poor political will, policy inconsistency, and weak regulatory enforcement
options.B: Because there are too many qualified nurses
options.C: Due to a lack of patients needing care
options.D: Because medical technology is too advanced

explanation: Nigeria frequently struggles with policy implementation due to poor political will, policy inconsistency across successive administrations, and weak regulatory enforcement. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h2)

question: What did the 2001 Abuja Declaration recommend regarding the national budget?

options.A: Allocating at least 5% to the defense sector
options.B: Allocating at least 15% of the annual budget to the health sector
options.C: Eliminating all taxes on medical supplies
options.D: Relying entirely on foreign loans for health

explanation: The Abuja Declaration recommended allocating at least 15% of the annual national budget to the health sector. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is a direct consequence of inadequate budgetary funding in the Nigerian health sector?

options.A: Surplus medical equipment in all clinics
options.B: Dilapidated infrastructure and shortages of essential medicines
options.C: Increased salaries for all healthcare workers
options.D: Universal free healthcare for every citizen

explanation: Inadequate budgetary funding leads to dilapidated infrastructure, shortages of essential medicines, obsolete diagnostic equipment, and poor remuneration. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h3)

question: How do impoverished individuals typically respond to out-of-pocket healthcare financing when illness occurs?

options.A: They immediately seek advanced private care
options.B: They delay seeking care until conditions reach advanced stages

explanation: Impoverished individuals often delay seeking care until conditions reach advanced or emergency stages due to out-of-pocket payment barriers. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is a major consequence of income inequality regarding healthcare access in Nigeria?

options.A: Equal distribution of medical doctors across all regions
options.B: Wealthy citizens accessing private care while the poor rely on underfunded public centers
options.C: Elimination of all public health disparities
options.D: Free insurance coverage for all low-income families

explanation: Income inequality means wealthy citizens can afford private care while the poor rely on underfunded and underequipped public primary health centers. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is a consistent benefit of higher levels of education regarding health?

options.B: Better health literacy and improved disease prevention behaviors

explanation: Higher levels of education are associated with better health literacy, enabling individuals to understand disease prevention and make informed health decisions. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h5)

question: How should nurses adapt their practice when dealing with patients who have low health literacy?

options.A: Use complex medical jargon to impress the patient
options.C: Tailor education using simple language, visual aids, and local dialects
options.D: Refer the patient immediately to a foreign hospital

explanation: Health education must be tailored to the literacy level of the patient, utilizing simple language, visual aids, and local dialects for clear communication. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why is a stable electricity supply critical in healthcare facilities?

options.A: Only for turning on office air conditioners
options.B: For operating diagnostic machines, preserving vaccines, and lighting operating theaters
options.C: To decrease the number of admitted patients
options.D: To eliminate the need for nursing staff

explanation: A stable electricity supply is critical for operating diagnostic machines, preserving vaccines, lighting operating theaters, and sterilizing equipment. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h6)

question: How do poor transportation networks and bad roads impact rural healthcare delivery in Nigeria?

options.A: They make it easier to transfer patients to tertiary centers
options.B: They create severe geographical barriers preventing patients from reaching facilities during emergencies
options.C: They reduce the cost of ambulance services
options.D: They ensure timely delivery of medical supplies

explanation: Bad road networks and lack of functional transport create severe geographical barriers, preventing rural dwellers from reaching facilities during emergencies. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following factors contributes significantly to high maternal and under-five mortality in Nigeria?

options.B: Poverty, early marriage, and inadequate antenatal care
options.D: An overabundance of skilled birth attendants

explanation: High rates of maternal and child mortality are driven by factors such as poverty, early marriage, low female literacy, and inadequate antenatal care. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h7)

question: What role do nurses and midwives play as frontline workers in maternal and child health?

options.A: They rely solely on clinical interventions without community engagement
options.B: They incorporate targeted health promotion, community outreach, and empowerment strategies
options.C: They encourage early marriage and discourage antenatal visits
options.D: They restrict care only to wealthy patients

explanation: Nurses and midwives must incorporate targeted health promotion, community outreach, and empowerment strategies alongside clinical care. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is meant by the term 'brain drain' in the context of the Nigerian health workforce?

options.A: The training of more medical specialists locally
options.B: The mass migration of skilled health professionals to developed countries
options.C: The retirement of elderly nurses from service
options.D: The shift from clinical nursing to administrative roles

explanation: Brain drain refers to the mass migration of skilled nurses, doctors, and health professionals to developed countries in search of better conditions. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h8)

question: What is a direct clinical consequence of brain drain on local health facilities in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive number of nursing staff per shift
options.B: Dangerously high nurse-to-patient ratios and severe staff burnout
options.D: A surplus of medical resources and equipment

explanation: The exodus of staff leaves local health facilities critically understaffed, resulting in high nurse-to-patient ratios and severe burnout. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h8)

question: Beyond traditional bedside care, what expanded roles should Nigerian nurses embrace?

options.A: Patient advocates, community educators, and health policy contributors
options.B: Hospital financiers and political campaign managers

explanation: Nurses must transcend traditional bedside care to embrace roles as patient advocates, community educators, and health policy contributors. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h9)

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand how social and political factors intersect with health?

options.A: To ensure patients pay higher hospital bills
options.B: To design holistic care plans that account for a patient's social reality
options.C: To avoid providing direct patient care
options.D: To replace physicians in diagnosing diseases

explanation: Understanding these intersections allows nurses to design holistic care plans that account for a patient's social reality and financial constraints. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h9)
